hook.line: When you half know something, you do not state it, you offer it up and let the other person say yes or no. Spanish has a polite phrase for exactly that, and you will hear it all over Bogotá.
hook.es: Tengo entendido que Altamira compró el edificio de al lado.
hook.en: I understand that Altamira bought the building next door.

examples.es: Tengo entendido que se aplazó la reunión.
examples.en: I understand that the meeting was postponed.

examples.es: Tengo entendido que Altamira compró el edificio de al lado.
examples.en: I understand that Altamira bought the building next door.

examples.es: Supe por Vale que Tomás se va a Canadá.
examples.en: I heard from Vale that Tomás is going to Canada.

examples.es: Me contaron que el café cierra en diciembre.
examples.en: I was told that the café closes in December.

examples.es: Nos contaron que el funcionario viajó a Miami.
examples.en: We were told that the official travelled to Miami.

examples.es: Tengo entendido que usted es el dueño del café, ¿verdad?
examples.en: I understand that you are the owner of the café, is that right? (formal)

rule:
Say *Tengo entendido que…* and then what you heard. It is not a question, but it invites a yes or a no, and it keeps the claim at arm's length.

Other ways to say where the news came from:
*Me contaron que…* (someone told me)
*Supe por Marta que…* (I heard it from Marta)

After all of these the news stays in the normal tense, with no special mood. Change the person on *tener*: *tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos*. *Entendido* never changes.
smallPrint: Teachers call this reporting without vouching: you pass on the news but do not guarantee it.

readAndPick.es: Tengo entendido que Rosa vendió el café.
options: I understand that Rosa sold the café.
I understand that Rosa will sell the café.
Rosa understands that I sold the café.

readAndPick.es: Me contaron que Tomás se va.
options: I told them that Tomás is leaving.
We were told that Tomás is leaving.
I was told that Tomás is leaving.

readAndPick.es: Nos contaron que cerraron la calle.
options: We were told that they closed the street.
I was told that they closed the street.
We told them that they closed the street.

readAndPick.es: Supe por Mariana que viajó a Miami.
options: Mariana heard from me that she travelled to Miami.
I heard from Mariana that she travelled to Miami.
You heard from Mariana that she travelled to Miami.

readAndPick.es: Tiene entendido que hay un juez.
options: I understand that there is a judge.
We understand that there is a judge.
She understands that there is a judge.

readAndPick.es: Tenemos entendido que la reunión se aplazó.
options: We understand that the meeting was postponed.
I understand that the meeting was postponed.
They understand that the meeting was postponed.

readAndPick.es: Supiste por Hernando que cierran el café.
options: I heard from Hernando that they are closing the café.
You heard from Hernando that they are closing the café.
He heard from you that they are closing the café.

readAndPick.es: Tengo entendido que no cierran el café.
options: I understand that they are closing the café.
I do not understand why they are closing the café.
I understand that they are not closing the café.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ que el café cierra en diciembre.* (*Me contaron* or *Me contó*) I was told that the café closes in December.
yourTurn.answer: Me contaron que el café cierra en diciembre.
yourTurn.why: *Me contaron* is the unnamed "people told me".

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Supe ___ Vale que Tomás se va.* (*por* or *de*) I heard from Vale that Tomás is leaving.
yourTurn.answer: Supe por Vale que Tomás se va.
yourTurn.why: The person you heard it from comes after *por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I understand that Altamira bought the building.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo entendido que Altamira compró el edificio.
yourTurn.why: *Tengo entendido que* opens the claim, then the news follows in its normal tense.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to the owner (formal): I understand that you are the owner.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo entendido que usted es el dueño.
accept: Tengo entendido que usted es la dueña.
yourTurn.why: The phrase stays the same with a formal *usted*; only the news changes.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We were told that the senator travelled to Miami.
yourTurn.answer: Nos contaron que el senador viajó a Miami.
yourTurn.why: *Nos contaron* is the *we* version of "someone told us".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Tengo entendido que el café cierra en diciembre.*
yourTurn.answer: Tengo entendido que el café no cierra en diciembre.
yourTurn.why: The *no* goes in the news, not before *tengo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Change to *we*: *Tengo entendido que Rosa vendió el café.*
yourTurn.answer: Tenemos entendido que Rosa vendió el café.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo entendido de que se aplazó la reunión.
pitfalls.right: Tengo entendido que se aplazó la reunión.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "I understand of" nothing, and neither does Spanish: *que* follows straight on.

pitfalls.wrong: Supe de Vale que Tomás se va.
pitfalls.right: Supe por Vale que Tomás se va.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For who told you, use *por*, not *de*.
Almost. You are reporting something you take as true, so no special mood: just *es*.

personal: Think of a rumour you have heard lately, about your work, your street or your family. Say it back with *Tengo entendido que…* and wait for someone to confirm it.
